note: The gallery's own seven places with NO authored geometry: a region, a box each stating only what it is, one pinned corner, a seam per connection stating which face of `a` it is on and where along that face the crossing sits (the compiler derives every other corner and every sill — spec-0059), the rock and the sky the whole owns, an `open` fill over a generated heightmap (`terrain/site.png`: every column's surface at `54 + v × 15 / 255`, drawn from the formula `63` north of the halls' south wall, stepping to `60` beyond it and to `55` at the southern edge, one course lower in every other eight-column band — no seed, so the image is the formula), eight comparisons holding all of it to its own written brief — and the blockout the engine derives from all of that. An overlay rather than primary surface because a campaign has ONE placement authority: the primary seats prefab pieces with `areas[]`, and this point of the same campaign hands the space to the plan, which is why it also carries its own world, cast, quest layer and translations. Everything a body meets in it is derived — the floors it walks, the doors it is stopped by, the stair it climbs, the anchors the quests bind to — so what this overlay proves is that the unchanged quest, gate and shortcut machinery lands on massing nobody authored and does not know the difference. Every one of its seven places is DETAILED (spec-0050), because a stand-in never ships and the point must be stageable, and each owns its outside (spec-0098): `node/exit` is filled by a hand-built piece the generator writes to exactly the frame the plan gives that place — a paved court on a plinth faced in stone down to the terrain, its ring open on the three sides it does not share; `node/annex`, whose box declares a nine-course roof with one cell of eaves, is filled with a program that draws its own walls and a stepped gable; and the halls, the loft, the undercroft and the causeway each with a plain program (`programs/<place>.json`) — a stone shell around the play space, a lantern-lit lid, an opening cut at every seam the place owns or answers, the near hall's three barred doors and its reliquary grille shipped as gates, the far hall's flight up to the loft's door, the undercroft's flight up through the far hall's floor, and its ladder up through the near hall's — the `climb` the undercroft hangs and the near hall tops in its own hole (spec-0099). ONE VERB (spec-0058) writes each: `delvec detail` reads the allocation itself, binds it into the program, expands it at the frame, voids every cell the place does not own, runs every gate before any file is written, freezes the piece and writes the row; the `detail-plan` that binds them carries no coordinate, no extent and no offset, and every program row is written by the tool, never by hand. An eighth place, `node/beacon`, is scenery (`reached: false`, spec-0098 §14): a sealed stone beacon on the open ground south-west of the yard, built to be seen and never entered, detailed like every other place and proven by the battery NOT reached. The declared vista from the near hall to the loft passes through a window in each wall at head height. It is one of the two places a horizon that builds terrain can be written, and which two is structural rather than a filing decision: a surround rings a declared extent, and exactly two documents declare one — this plan's `region`, and the single prefab a one-area campaign binds, which is what the `valley-site` overlay is. The primary is neither: it places TWO areas on the compiler's stride, so `{base: "valley"}` on it is `DW0855` and has its probe beside this. The mountains here are built around the same rectangle the boxes are allocated inside, which is what makes the landform something a later detail pass cannot move.
